summary: A free, compact nature and learning stop inside Wachirabenchathat (Rot Fai) Park, with a walk-through butterfly enclosure and exhibits about insect life cycles. It pairs well with the adjoining Chatuchak park cluster, though its current opening schedule should be reconfirmed before making a special trip.
whyGo: See live butterflies in a planted, open-air dome and learn about their life cycle and host plants.
Add a shaded, low-cost stop to a visit to Rot Fai Park, Queen Sirikit Park or the Chatuchak area.
bestFor: Families and visitors interested in insects, plants or a gentle break from markets and city streets.
People already exploring the northern park cluster who can keep plans flexible.
skipIf: You need a guaranteed attraction on a Monday or cannot verify operating status on your date.
You expect a large museum or a long indoor visit; this is a small garden and learning stop.
duration: Allow about 30–60 minutes as a planning estimate, plus time to walk through the large park to reach it.
cost: Free admission according to the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration and Tourism Authority of Thailand. Budget for transport and any separate park activities.
hours: BMA's Chatuchak Park portal lists daily except Monday, 08:30–16:30; TAT lists Tuesday–Sunday and public holidays at the same hours. A separate Bangkok Learning City listing says daily, so verify directly before visiting, especially on Mondays or public holidays.
bestTime: Visit in daylight, preferably late morning on a sunny day if butterfly activity matters; this timing is a practical suggestion, not a guaranteed seasonal pattern. Avoid arriving close to the 16:30 listed closing time.
gettingThere: The garden is within Wachirabenchathat (Rot Fai) Park on Kamphaeng Phet 3 Road, connected to the Chatuchak and Queen Sirikit park grounds. BTS Mo Chit and MRT Chatuchak Park are useful transit points for the park cluster; expect a substantial walk inside the park. Use a map pin for the garden entrance rather than assuming the nearest station is at its door.
booking: Walk-in visitors register at the garden. BMA says group visits require a written request about 5–7 working days ahead; contact the garden at +66 2 272 4359. No general ticket reservation is indicated.
accessibility: The enclosure and park setting involve walking; current step-free access, path surfaces, seating and accessible toilets are not documented in the sources checked. Contact the operator for mobility-specific details before relying on access.
practicalTips: Check the BMA park page or call +66 2 272 4359 shortly before setting out; published schedules differ on Monday opening.
Wear comfortable shoes and bring water; the garden sits within a large park and is not at the transit station entrance.
Treat butterflies as living wildlife: avoid touching or feeding them, and follow any on-site instructions.
decemberNotes: December is a comfortable time for the surrounding park, but the garden is a living exhibit and butterfly activity can vary with weather and conditions. No special December 2026 programme was confirmed. Check opening arrangements close to the visit, including any public-holiday schedule.
uncertainties: The BMA Chatuchak Park page gives Monday closure, while another BMA city listing says daily; TAT says Tuesday–Sunday plus public holidays. Confirm the exact date directly.
No December 2026 event calendar or current butterfly/species count was verified.
Accessibility details for the enclosure and visitor facilities were not available in the sources checked.
